title: KV micro-shard introspective compression probe (FP8/INT8/INT4) + streaming-quality callbacks
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Background: As we push for denser GPU packing and lower per-token cost, KV cache accounts for a significant fraction of peak memory on long-context workloads. Prior work looked at blockwise and tiered quantization; this probe evaluates a micro-shard approach where small contiguous KV slices (micro-shards) are compressed with differing formats (FP8, INT8, INT4) based on an introspective fidelity signal. The goal is to preserve end-to-end generation quality while reducing memory pressure during continuous batching and heavy multi-tenant packing.

Hypothesis: Most tokens in live traffic contribute low marginal signal to future token probabilities; applying finer-grained micro-shard quantization guided by a per-shard SNR-like heuristic will reduce GPU memory by ~20-35% with <0.5% relative regression in logprob-per-token for top-1 generations on our internal eval suite.

Goals:
- Implement micro-shard encoding layer and runtime fallback in the serving runtime.
- Measure memory reduction, latency tail impact under continuous batching, and quality regressions across FP8/INT8/INT4 mixes.
- Define safe rollout thresholds and automated rollback for user-visible regressions.

Experiment design (technical):
1) Micro-shard definition: shard size = 64 token-steps x 128 hidden dims (configurable). Each cached KV slice is partitioned into micro-shards.
2) Fidelity signal: compute fast per-shard metric approximating contribution (squared l2 of recent attention context projection scaled by token recency + token rarity factor). Signal computed during inference with minimal overhead (<2% CPU).
3) Encoding tiers: keep (FP16/FP32), FP8 (E4M3-like), INT8 asymmetric, INT4 with 4-bit block quant plus scale per micro-shard.
4) Runtime policy: initially classify shards into three bands (high/medium/low) -> keep/FP8/INT8/INT4 fallback. Add a hot-preservation rule for last N steps.
5) Fallback: if per-request generation logprob drops > threshold vs baseline, uncompress relevant shards synchronously (hotpath) and mark shard hot for next M requests.

Datasets & workloads:
- Internal long-context suite (LLM-long-2k, synthetic recency traces)
- Production-sampled anonymized tails for 7 days (stored dashboards)
- Strategic eval prompts (dialog completion, code synthesis, retrieval-augmented generation)

Metrics:
- Memory: peak KV alloc per-model (MB), mean GPU resident set under 95th percentile batching pressure
- Latency: median and p99 per-token generation time under continuous batching regimes (1k-10k QPS simulated)
- Quality: delta in average token logprob, pass@k on code tests, and human evaluation samples for subjective fluency (small set)
- Stability: frequency of runtime fallback events and related tail latency spikes
- Cost proxy: estimated token cost reduction per hour under typical load

Gating & acceptance criteria:
- Memory: >=20% median KV memory reduction on 2k context experiments without violating GPU allocation limits in 99% of simulated runs
- Quality: <0.5% relative degradation in mean logprob and no >1.5% regressions on any critical eval family (code completion, legal text)
- Latency: p99 per-token increase <15ms attributable to decompression or fallback events
- Operational: fallback rate <0.1% of requests and no repeated oscillation between compressed/uncompressed states

Implementation notes & infra changes:
- Add per-micro-shard metadata to the KV header (16 bytes) for fast classification; benchmark header overhead.
- New kernel paths for INT8/INT4 dequant on the GPU with vectorized LUTs; prioritize CUDA kernels but provide CPU fallback for Private installs.
- Telemetry hooks: per-shard compression type, fidelity score, fallback counter emitted to Console (new dashboards).
- Rollout plan: start on canary cluster with synthetic replay, then 1% production traffic, monitor, ramp.

Risks and mitigations:
- Quality cliffs for rare tokens: maintain hot-preservation for recent tokens and add cohort-aware safelist for named entities.
- Latency spikes from synchronous decompression: implement amortized background warmup and limit synchronous decompression to user-visible thresholds.
- Complexity in debugging: include a deterministic reproducer and a debug mode that logs per-shard stats for failing requests.

Open questions:
- Optimal micro-shard size tradeoff between metadata overhead and fidelity granularity.
- Best heuristic for token rarity that generalizes across languages.
- Whether INT4 block quant with per-block scale is superior to per-shard asymmetric INT4 with offset.

Next steps:
- Spike: implement encoding/decoding kernel prototypes (ETA 6d).
- Bench: run controlled replay of 4M tokens and produce memory/quality matrix (ETA 8d).
- Review: sync with Applied ML for evaluation thresholds and with Console for telemetry spec (ETA 3d).

Artifacts: design doc (Confluence), prototype PR, dashboard mockups listed below in links.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Implementation merged behind feature flag; 2) Canary run shows >=20% KV memory reduction and quality within thresholds; 3) Monitoring dashboard created with alerts for fallback rate and quality regressions; 4) Rollout playbook documented in Confluence with rollback steps.
